recommendations: Upgrade the Colab COLMAP step to COLMAP >=4.0.0 (ideally 4.1.1, released 2026-07-17) instead of hand-installing a separate GLOMAP binary — GLOMAP's own repo (github.com/colmap/glomap) was archived/deprecated on 2026-03-09 with the note it is 'fully migrated to COLMAP, where GLOMAP functionality is exposed as the global mapper'. Drop any GLOMAP-specific install step from the pipeline and just call COLMAP's `--Mapper.ba_global_use_pba`/global mapper mode.

Keep (don't remove) the existing ffmpeg perspective-reframe/cubemap-split step for the still-photo path. COLMAP 4.1.0's new native spherical/equirectangular camera model is explicitly documented as 'generally faster but less accurate than rendering perspective views' — wrong tradeoff when you only have 20 sparse stills and need every match to count, especially around thin bridge railings/trusses that suffer at equirect poles.

For splitting each of the 20 equirectangular JPGs, adopt the nerfstudio ns-process-data convention rather than a plain 6-face 90° cube: 8 faces at 120° FOV or 14 faces at 110° FOV, at pitches [-45,0,45]. This produces ~160-280 well-overlapping perspective frames from 20 panoramas, giving COLMAP's exhaustive matcher enough shared coverage to close the loop around the bridge and roadway. Use `ns-process-data images --camera-type equirectangular --images-per-equirect 14` directly, or the underlying py360convert library (pip install py360convert) if you want the split step to stay inside Orbit Studio's own scripts rather than depend on nerfstudio.

Switch feature extraction/matching in the Colab step to COLMAP's built-in ALIKED (via ONNX) + LightGlue (via ONNX) path, added natively in COLMAP 4.0.0 (2026-03-14) — this removes the need to vendor the separate hloc toolbox (whose last tagged release, v1.4, is from July 2024; ALIKED/XFeat support lives only on hloc's unreleased master via open PRs like #441). Keep classic SIFT + exhaustive matching as an automatic fallback if ALIKED/LightGlue produce a broken/disconnected reconstruction on the repetitive pavement/asphalt texture around the bridge.

Do not add OpenMVG or SphereSfM (json87/SphereSfM) to the pipeline. OpenMVG's 'Spherical' camera is reported by its own maintainers as not true equirectangular projection, with the correct model (Spherical_Equirectangular) still an open, unresolved GitHub issue (#1045) after years. SphereSfM is a maintained but niche COLMAP fork (last release 2025-08-18) that adds deployment risk versus mainline COLMAP now shipping native spherical support directly.

After matching, run COLMAP's integrated global mapper (ex-GLOMAP) first for speed, but keep the incremental mapper as an automatic retry path if global mapper output looks degenerate — GLOMAP's own paper and COLMAP's rotation-averaging robustification notes (4.1.0 changelog: 'Robustified gravity-aligned rotation averaging against 180-degree flips') both flag global SfM's known failure mode on small/structured loop scenes, which a 20-photo bridge loop is exactly.
slice: Structure-from-motion for 360 imagery in 2026 (Orbit Studio research)
summary: The SfM-for-360 landscape consolidated sharply into COLMAP itself in 2026. GLOMAP, the standalone fast global-SfM pipeline, was archived on 2026-03-09 after being fully merged into COLMAP 4.0.0 (2026-03-14) as a first-class 'global mapper' mode, alongside natively integrated ALIKED (via ONNX) feature extraction and LightGlue (via ONNX) matching for both SIFT and ALIKED. COLMAP 4.1.0 (2026-06-26) then added native spherical/equirectangular and Enhanced Unified Camera Model (EUCM) support plus the Caspar GPU bundle-adjustment backend (1-2 orders of magnitude faster than Ceres-CUDA); 4.1.1 (2026-07-17) is the current stable point release. Critically, COLMAP's own docs describe native equirectangular reconstruction as faster but less accurate than the classic cubemap/perspective-split approach, so for a sparse 20-photo dataset the traditional split-then-SfM workflow remains the safer choice. Nerfstudio's ns-process-data (`--camera-type equirectangular --images-per-equirect 8|14`, FOV 120deg/110deg with pitch bounds [-45,0,45]) is the closest thing to a standardized, actively-maintained splitting tool, and its main equirect artifact bug (issue #3445) is closed. hloc, by contrast, hasn't cut a tagged release since v1.4 (July 2024); its ALIKED/XFeat support lives on an unreleased master branch, making COLMAP's own native ALIKED+LightGlue integration the more current path. OpenMVG's spherical camera model is widely reported as not truly equirectangular and unresolved for years; SphereSfM (json87) is a maintained but niche research fork (last release 2025-08-18). Net: COLMAP 4.1.x alone, fed cubemap-split stills, is now the most reliable open-source pose-recovery path.

uncertainties: The exact COLMAP version where the spherical/equirectangular camera model first landed is inconsistent across sources: one GitHub issue (#3595, opened 2025-08-26) attributes it to COLMAP 3.12, while release notes and changelog fetches attribute the 'native reconstruction without rendering to perspective' framing to 4.1.0 (2026-06-26). Likely 3.12 added a basic spherical camera model usable via pycolmap, and 4.1.0 made it more complete/native, but this could not be fully disambiguated from available fetches.

Whether COLMAP's GUI (as of the current 4.1.1, 2026-07-17) now exposes the spherical camera model as a selectable option, versus still requiring the Python/pycolmap scripting path, is unconfirmed — the only issue found on this (#3595) was opened in August 2025 with no visible maintainer resolution in the fetched content.
hloc's exact master-branch (unreleased) support status for ALIKED and XFeat+LighterGlue (PR #441) as of July 2026 could not be confirmed as merged vs. still open/in-review.

No single authoritative 'best practice' document was found specifying an optimal face count/FOV/overlap specifically for splitting STILL equirectangular photos (as opposed to video frames) for SfM; the two concrete conventions found (nerfstudio's 8-or-14-face scheme and a generic '90 deg cube faces expanded to ~95 deg for overlap' pattern from cubemap-literature/GitHub issue discussion) are both plausible but not COLMAP-endorsed standards for this exact use case.

Could not confirm whether pycolmap's current PyPI release (as installable in a fresh Google Colab T4 notebook in July 2026) already wraps COLMAP 4.1.x's native spherical camera model and Caspar GPU backend, or lags behind the C++ releases.
